draft.title: Kublai Khan and the empire's decline
card: Kublai Khan was a grandson of Genghis Khan. He conquered China, which had been ruled by the Song dynasty, and in 1271 founded the Yuan dynasty there.
Kublai ruled as Great Khan from his capital at Khanbaliq, which is now Beijing. He used Chinese officials and ideas to help rule China, but he gave many top jobs to foreigners.

The empire was too large for one ruler to control. After a struggle over who should rule, it split into four separate realms, each ruled by a khan and called a khanate. The khanates often became rivals.
The Yuan dynasty was one of these realms. Rebellions grew in China, and in 1368 the Yuan were driven out and the Ming dynasty began.
draft.remember: Kublai Khan founded the Yuan dynasty, but a huge empire split into rival khanates, and the Yuan fell in 1368.

a.q: Why did the Mongol Empire break into separate khanates?
opts: It was too big to control, and rulers fought over power
Kublai Khan gave each khanate to a Chinese emperor
The Song dynasty defeated the Mongol armies everywhere
Its soldiers refused to serve once Genghis Khan died
a.why: The empire stretched across a vast area, and after a struggle over who should rule it divided into khanates that became rivals. The Song dynasty did not defeat the Mongols, since Kublai Khan conquered it.
a.clue: Think about the size of the empire and who should rule it.

b.q: In 1368, rebels drove the Yuan rulers out of China. What does this show about the Mongol Empire by then?
opts: It had split into realms, and the Yuan was only one of them
It was still one empire, ruled by a single Great Khan
It had split because Kublai Khan failed to conquer China
It had lost China, and every khanate fell in the same year
b.why: By 1368 the empire was divided into separate khanates, and the Yuan was only one of them. Its fall ended Mongol rule in China, not in the other khanates. Kublai Khan had conquered China, so he did not fail to do so.
b.clue: Was the Yuan the whole empire, or one part of it?

a.best: It was too big to control, and rulers fought over power

b.best: It had split into realms, and the Yuan was only one of them

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about the size of the empire and who should rule it' maps directly onto the two halves of the right option, so a student can match the words without knowing the idea.
The clue 'Was the Yuan the whole empire, or one part of it?' restates the right option ('the Yuan was only one of them'), which gives the answer away.
